Fun little story. My girlfriend’s aunt lives in a really cute old stone house in Normandy they fixed up themselves. While they were renovating the house there was a pile of dirt/old canvas/burlap in the shed and she noticed a jacket in it. She took out the jacket and it turned out to be an old Mont Saint Michel jacket. Not sure how old it is but it is OLD. The previous owner had done some patchwork, it’s gotten beautifully faded, every button is different, it’s an art piece and has so much history embedded into it. I knew the brand before this happened but always thought it was too expensive. This story made me bite the bullet and buy one and swore to myself that I would wear it until it looked like that

I have a strong preference for chore coats, barn jackets, and utility jackets; approximately 90% of my outerwear falls into one of these three categories.  However, what I appreciate most about these jackets is the quality of their tailoring and the attention to detail. Only those jackets with interesting or unique details are added to my collection.

I am particularly drawn to features such as corduroy trims, flannel linings, snaps, double zippers, action backs, vented backs, body drawstrings, adjustable cuffs, elbow patches, triple stitching, durable materials, and machine washability.

To be honest, I was unfamiliar with most of the brands mentioned in the video, except for Carhartt and Levi's. My personal preferences lean towards brands like Orvis, L. L. Bean, Brooks Brothers, Patagonia, travelsmith, Pendleton, hunting or fishing jackets, and vintage brands.

Every item should have a purpose and perform its function efficiently, so that its use is seamless and unobtrusive; otherwise, it becomes a distraction.  It is not the objects themselves that make us unique and interesting, but rather, it is our ability to give those objects purpose and use them effectively in our work.  Whether it's boots or hats, if we're going to spend more than the average person, let's make it interesting and distinctive.

Chore, barn it doesn't matter because they have a similar silhouette and structure, some are like hybrid blazer/chore coats..my Scotch and Soda has the same herringbone Twill weave like the buck Mason, even the color is kind of similar, except mine is a sun faded, olive green, with details and Lines that look more like the blazer,albeit a casual one. It has a false pocket on the right side, and three pockets, two bottom ones with flaps and buttons that look awesome because they are at an angle, the one left chest pocket is simple, but not ordinary the collar looks great standing up or down like a typical sport coat with lapel's, all of those jackets seem very plain, different colors, but mostly ordinary looking. That royal blue color is not a great color choice regardless if it's popular. There's just something about the tone and temperature of that blue that I don't like. I like faded, worn in, indigo jackets with a great patina, I rarely buy new clothes because they look dull, denim should look lived in and of course, not all denim is the same, my G star is fantastic, Japanese.selvedge denim faded with a great patina and 3D details. All my jackets were purchased online for less than $60 each, but they look far more expensive. Today I'm getting my camouflage blue.chore coat by Denham, yet another Dutch designer with premium Japanese denim that looks fantastic, so unique, and of course, not so easy to style unless you have a good sense of color, chemistry, and understanding how to mix patterns, plaids, and solids, definitely not boring, definitely unique and rare, that's how I choose my jackets, I don't want other people wearing the same things. I always go for unique and rare items that you won't see other people wearing, so you have your own sense of style, make it look, effortless, don't try too hard to create outfits because they tend to look boring, usually mostly solid colors, no patterns, no plaids, can be really boring, nice, but bland. Being an artist definitely helps, just be more creative. People create your own personal style with character and try not to be boring.
